THE SAFE · OFFLINE PRIVATE-KEY ANCHOR

Keys that live where the internet can't follow

Vault is the always-offline half of the pair. It holds your private key in Keystore TEE, has no INTERNET permission at all, and signs your identity only when another device asks — across the room, over signed IPC, never over the wire.

↓ Download Vault
Vault offline · the private-key safe
Why offline

Breach a server, take the ciphertext. There are no keys in the breach.

Most "encrypted" apps put routing and key custody in the same trust zone. Vault ends the gamble the primitive way: the device that holds keys physically cannot reach the network.

Zero Internet permission

The Android manifest declares no INTERNET permission. Even a malicious caller cannot make Vault phone home.

TEE / DRM sealed seed

The device seed is anchored in hardware-backed Keystore TEE/DRM, not in files a process can read.

Signs, doesn't store

Identity signatures are produced on demand and delegated to the always-online Engine over signed IPC callbacks.

Zero egress

Nothing leaves the device unless you approve a signature. Nothing of value can be exfiltrated.
